title: Maximum Coin Collection
statement:
A two-lane road is divided into miles `0` to `n - 1`. Driving mile `i` in lane 1 changes your coin total by `lane1[i]`, and driving it in lane 2 changes it by `lane2[i]`; a negative value is a toll that takes coins away.

You get on the road at the start of any mile and get off after any mile at or after it, so you drive one contiguous, non-empty run of miles. You always get on in lane 1 and may change lanes at most twice. A change happens between two miles, or right as you get on, so every mile you drive counts in exactly one lane. In other words, the miles you drive are, in order: some in lane 1, then some in lane 2, then some in lane 1 again, where any of the three groups may be empty.

Return the largest coin total you can finish with. You must drive at least one mile, so the answer may be negative.
notes:
## Intuition

The miles you drive form one block whose lanes go lane 1, lane 2, lane 1, with any part possibly empty. A brute force tries every block and both switch points inside it: O(n⁴) combinations even with prefix sums.

Instead, treat the drive as a state machine with three states: no switch yet (lane 1), one switch (lane 2) and two switches (lane 1 again). Sweep the road once, keeping for each state the best total of a drive that ends at the current mile in that state. It is Kadane's maximum subarray with three states instead of one.

## Approach

1. Start `noSwitch`, `oneSwitch`, `twoSwitches` and `best` at `-Infinity`: no drive has ended yet.
2. For each mile `i`, from the last state back to the first:
   - `twoSwitches`: continue in lane 1, or come back from lane 2 now; add `lane1[i]`.
   - `oneSwitch`: continue in lane 2, move over from lane 1 now, or get on here and switch at once (the `0`); add `lane2[i]`.
   - `noSwitch`: continue in lane 1, or get on here (the `0`); add `lane1[i]`.
3. Each state is now a real drive ending at mile `i`, so fold all three into `best`.
4. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`lane1 = [1, -2, -10, 3]`, `lane2 = [-5, 10, 0, 1]`:

| `i` | `noSwitch` | `oneSwitch` | `twoSwitches` | `best` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | -5 | -Infinity | 1 |
| 1 | -1 | max(-5, 1, 0) + 10 = 11 | -7 | 11 |
| 2 | -10 | 11 | max(-7, 11) - 10 = 1 | 11 |
| 3 | 3 | 12 | max(1, 11) + 3 = 14 | 14 |

The `14` is mile 0 in lane 1, miles 1 and 2 in lane 2, and mile 3 back in lane 1.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per mile.
- Space: O(1): four numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Update `twoSwitches`, then `oneSwitch`, then `noSwitch` (or use temporaries); in the other order a state reads a value that already includes mile `i`.
- At least one mile must be driven, so start from `-Infinity`, not 0: in Example 5 the answer is `-2`.
- Switching right as you get on is allowed, so a drive may start in lane 2: that is the `0` in `oneSwitch`'s max, and Example 3 needs it.
- Totals can reach about 10^14, so Java and C need a 64-bit `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `noSwitch` | best total of a drive ending at mile `i` in lane 1 with no switch |
| `oneSwitch` | best total of a drive ending at mile `i` in lane 2 after one switch |
| `twoSwitches` | best total of a drive ending at mile `i` back in lane 1 after two switches |
| `best` | best total of any drive seen so far |
| `i` | the current mile |

narration.3: No drive has ended yet, so every state starts at -Infinity.
narration.6: The best total of any drive so far; it is replaced as soon as mile 0 is driven.
narration.7: Visit the miles from left to right.
narration.9: Two switches used, back in lane 1: either keep driving in lane 1, or come back from lane 2 at this mile.
narration.10: One switch used, in lane 2: keep going in lane 2, move over from lane 1, or get on here and switch at once (the 0).
narration.11: No switch yet, in lane 1: extend the drive, or get on here with a fresh total (the 0).
narration.12: Each state is a real drive ending at this mile; keep the largest total seen.
narration.14: Return the best total over every drive.
